messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the test expects: In BasicParserTest.testOptionGroupLong, two options are added to an OptionGroup using only long names (“foo” and “bar”), then the parser is run with ["--bar"]. The test asserts that group.getSelected() returns "bar".
- Symptom from the bug report: “If the selected option hasn’t a short name, group.setSelected(option) has no effect.” This matches a failure where getSelected() remains null when choosing a long-only option.
- How OptionGroup stores and reports selection:
  - OptionGroup.addOption stores options in a map keyed by Option.getKey().
  - Option.getKey() returns longOpt when the short opt is null; otherwise it returns opt. This means the group is set up to use the long name as the key for long-only options.
  - OptionGroup.getSelected() simply returns the internal selected field.
- What goes wrong: The selection is never recorded for long-only options. This is consistent with a setSelected implementation that compares/assigns using option.getOpt() (the short name). For long-only options, option.getOpt() is null, so selected is either not updated or set to null. As a result, after parsing "--bar", OptionGroup.selected remains null, and group.getSelected() returns null instead of "bar".
- Chain of events causing the failure:
  1) Options group is created with two long-only options.
  2) During parse of "--bar", the parser identifies the corresponding Option and attempts to mark it as selected on its OptionGroup.
  3) OptionGroup.setSelected uses the short name (option.getOpt()) to record selection; since it’s a long-only option, getOpt() is null, so selection is not recorded.
  4) group.getSelected() returns null, causing the assertion expecting "bar" to fail.
- Why this is a logic bug: Elsewhere, OptionGroup consistently uses Option.getKey() for identification (addOption stores by getKey), which properly handles long-only options. setSelected is inconsistent by using getOpt() instead of getKey(), breaking long-only selection. The fix is to make selection tracking use option.getKey() (or explicitly use longOpt when short opt is null), so that long-only options set selected to their long name, fulfilling the test’s expectation.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
